deduped.title: Cross-tenant IDOR: /api/company/{company_id}/slds, /sessions and /sales-attention return another tenant's records to an ordinary customer admin (is_eg_admin false)
deduped.impact: Any signed-in customer admin who knows another company's UUID reads that tenant's facility names, work-order titles, account_id and sld_id — confidentiality breach across customers, with UUID knowledge the only barrier.
deduped.quote: Several `/api/company/{company_id}/…` endpoints **do not verify that `{company_id}` belongs to the caller**. A signed-in user of one tenant can read another tenant's facilities, work orders and sales data simply by substituting the other company's UUID in the path.

deduped.title: POST /ir_session/scope-preview accepts any sld_id with no caller-company check, so a demo-tenant user on their own host reads 84 acme assets plus room_label building PII

deduped.quote: It **fails**: a Company B user reads Company A's `eg-form-instance/by-session` data (with real `form_submission`) from their own host, and the session list is self-discovering.

deduped.quote: **NEW confirmed leak — `GET /api/sld/{id}` (singular).** A customer admin of EG-ACME (`is_eg_admin:false`) fetching Demo's SLD id `24eb08b1…` receives the **entire foreign SLD document**

deduped.impact: Non-admin roles are offered an edit affordance that cannot work, dead-ending on a permission card instead of being hidden or locked like the configs list, EG Forms and editor surfaces.

deduped.title: Work order Forms tab badge stays "Forms 1" after the last form instance is deleted (EGF-1) — only a page reload clears it, while the server already reports total: 0

deduped.title: Services procedure edit dialog styles the empty-by-design Forms field as a validation failure — red/error border plus "No forms recorded" while the listbox reads "No options"

deduped.quote: Cosmetic, but the label is **reused verbatim on the work order**, so it reaches customer-visible output. A `.trim()` on the interpolated value fixes it.

deduped.title: Build version is unanswerable from the UI: the sidebar badge reads V1.36 while the release panel advertises "Fixes in Web v1.39.1"
deduped.impact: A tester (or customer) cannot tell which build they are on, which cost this run real time and will cost the next person the same.
deduped.quote: the sidebar badge reads **V1.36**, but the release panel advertises *"Fixes in Web v1.39.1"* — the two disagree, which makes "is this build current?" unanswerable from the UI. Minor, but it cost me time here

deduped.title: Flipping an asset's shutdown rule to "Can never shut down" leaves its already-scheduled de-energized PM lines live and due, with nothing flagging the now-impossible schedule
deduped.impact: An asset that can never be shut down keeps showing de-energized PM work as due; the restriction is only consulted at apply time, so existing programs stay wrong until something rewrites them.
deduped.quote: both assets still held their full 4-line programs with all three de-energized lines still due; the restriction is only consulted when a program is applied ... Nothing flags a now-impossible schedule on an asset that can never be shut down.

deduped.title: An undated de-energized PM line keeps its outage-aligned due date after the shutdown restriction is relaxed, persisting a wrong due date until unrelated activity re-derives it

deduped.quote: the undated De-Energized Visual Inspection stayed at the outage-aligned 1 Mar 2029 (it has no anchor to re-derive from) ... it is a wrong due date that persists until unrelated activity fixes it, and the two lines disagree about which rule they follow.

deduped.title: The same four shutdown-restriction enum values are labelled with two different vocabularies - asset page says "Can never shut down", the bulk dialog says "Never"
deduped.area: Asset PM programs / shutdown restrictions UI
deduped.impact: One workflow presents two wordings for the same setting, so a user cannot be sure the bulk dialog's "Never" is the asset page's "Can never shut down".
deduped.quote: Same enum (`unrestricted`, `bypass`, `planned_shutdowns_only`, `never`), two vocabularies in one workflow.

deduped.impact: Searching "Criticality 2" on a Panelboard returns four rows with identical text, so a user cannot tell which standard's plan they are about to apply.
deduped.quote: Searching "Criticality 2" on a Panelboard returns four rows all reading "Panelboard (Generic) — Criticality 2 · Whole class · 4 services" ... Only the group header distinguishes them

deduped.title: No resolution ever reaches the applied state on QA - only proposed, accepted and superseded are observable
deduped.impact: The state that is supposed to close the loop when a break/fix form is submitted is unreachable, so an accepted-and-quoted fix never records as applied.
deduped.quote: Across every issue examined the statuses seen are `proposed`, `accepted` and `superseded`. `applied` is the state the ticket says an accepted resolution moves to when a break/fix form is submitted, and nothing on QA has got there

deduped.title: The disconnect-switch Manufacturer filter offers eight ANSI/UL standards documents as manufacturers (and they return real rows)
deduped.impact: A user picking a manufacturer is shown ANSI C37.06-1979 and UL 891 alongside ABB and GE; selecting a standard returns six real bus models, so the dropdown misrepresents the catalog's attribution. (Same defect also reported in the ZP-3937 verdict.)
deduped.quote: Eight of the fifteen entries offered in the Manufacturer filter are not manufacturers: **ANSI C37.06-1979, ANSI C37.06-1987, ANSI C37.06-1997, ANSI C37.16-1997, UL 347, UL 67, UL 845, UL 891**. Selecting ANSI C37.06-1979 returns six real rows

deduped.title: Bolted-pressure disconnect lineups are not findable by name - "bolted" and "PRESSURE" both return 0 rows for type=disconnect_switch
deduped.impact: One of the four device families this fix names as findable cannot be located by the words a user would type, so those switches stay unlinked.
deduped.quote: Neither "bolted" nor "PRESSURE" returns anything for `type=disconnect_switch`. They may be catalogued under a manufacturer's own product name, but a user searching the words in the ticket finds nothing.

deduped.title: The resolutions empty state still tells users to press "Suggest with AI", the button this change removed
deduped.impact: The one screen a user reaches when evaluation has not happened instructs them to click a control that no longer exists anywhere in the product.
deduped.quote: the one place a user lands when evaluation has not happened is also the one place that tells them to do something impossible. It is the only surviving occurrence of the phrase in the bundle.

deduped.title: Rejections on the procedures-v2 pm-plans routes surface as the platform's masked-404 (200 + SPA HTML) instead of the 403 the ticket specifies
deduped.impact: A foreign-tenant pm_standard_id on the covered-services picker, and a write against a not-owned standard (swap-service, matrix, POST /pm-plans), are both blocked but return 200 + SPA HTML rather than a typed 403/4xx JSON - safe in outcome, undebuggable for clients and a deviation from the documented contract.
deduped.quote: **But the mechanism is the platform's masked-404, not the clean `403` + message the ticket promises.**

deduped.title: The EG Forms bulk-export endpoint silently ignores unknown request keys, so a caller sending `format` instead of `output_format` gets a default PDF job started rather than a 400
deduped.impact: A client typo or version skew produces a silently wrong export (a billable PDF job) instead of an error; this same behaviour produced a false "DOCX accepted" reading during testing.
deduped.quote: the export endpoint reads **`output_format`**; an unknown key like `format` is silently ignored and the request falls through to a default PDF job.

deduped.title: Upload Anything "Start new upload" keeps the previous job's files staged, so adding one file shows five
deduped.impact: A user starting over unknowingly re-submits the previous run's images, paying for extraction on files they thought they had discarded.
deduped.quote: After the failed run I clicked *Start new upload* and added 1 file; the dialog showed **5** — the 4 previous images plus mine.

deduped.title: Deleting an asset leaves its issues behind still displaying the deleted asset in the Issues grid's Asset column
deduped.impact: The Issues list shows a dangling asset reference that can no longer be opened or acted on.
deduped.quote: After deleting `QA-CTL-SWB-01`, its issue still lists `QA-CTL-SWB-01` in the Asset column. Cosmetic, but the reference is dangling.

deduped.title: Site Walks entitlement is not enforced server-side: GET /api/site-walk/list answers HTTP 200 normally on a tenant that does not hold the site-walks feature
deduped.impact: The feature check exists only in the client, so any caller of /api/site-walk/* on an unentitled tenant is served rather than refused (no data exposure, but no server-side entitlement).
deduped.quote: **The backend is not feature-gated either.** `GET /api/site-walk/list` returns **HTTP 200** with a normal payload on the feature-less tenant

deduped.title: proposed_resolution is absent from the hand-maintained available_fields whitelist on all 8 issue report templates across 106 configs, so report authors cannot select it at all
deduped.impact: On the older DOCX-generation templates the field is not offerable in the builder (zero declarations, zero full-text hits), so those reports can never bind it even after the template gate is fixed.
deduped.quote: The `available_fields` whitelist gap below is real but affects only the OLD DOCX templates ... Keeping it as a separate low-priority ticket.

deduped.title: Issue-class property names are stored untrimmed and case-sensitive, so details_by_key carries duplicate/near-duplicate keys ("", "Problem Temp" vs "Problem Temp   ", "Replacement check 1" vs "replacement check 1")
deduped.impact: Any template keying details_by_key on a property name silently misses rows whose key differs by whitespace or case - the same silent-miss failure class the reporter hit.
deduped.quote: Any template keying `details_by_key` on these strings silently misses rows — same failure class the reporter hit. Recommend trimming/case-folding keys or keying on property id.

deduped.title: "Proposed Resolution" exists both as an issue-class property in details[] and as the top-level proposed_resolution column with different values, and the report builder gives no way to tell them apart
deduped.impact: A report author binding "Proposed Resolution" cannot know which of two different values they will get on the same issue.
deduped.quote: "Proposed Resolution" is BOTH an issue-class property in `details[]` (value e.g. `"Cable"`) AND the top-level free-text `proposed_resolution` column (e.g. `"Install 1.25\" bushing."`). Different values on the same issue. The builder gives an author no way to tell them apart.

deduped.title: Nameplate agent handles the same class of plate conflict two different ways - refuses to bind (no_match) for one manufacturer, silently binds the wrong voltage tier with only a warning for another (and raised nothing at all on an admittedly offset multi-tier plate)
deduped.impact: Identical review situations surface to the engineer as either "No SKM match" or a confident designation with an amber chip; CB8 bound a 25 kA frame with high confidence and no warning after noting the plate table was offset from SKM's data.
deduped.quote: Same class of plate conflict, two behaviours: E1.2 plates with a kA no E1.2 frame offers → refused (`no_match`, "identity contradiction"); HJ plate with a kA that exists only at another voltage tier → bound the kA-matching frame at the "wrong" tier + warning.

deduped.title: /api/skm-cable-library/insulation-classes only parses literal true/false for is_busway - ?is_busway=1 and =0 both return the full unscoped 32-item list with no error
deduped.area: Enum scoping / SKM cable library API
deduped.impact: Any HTTP client passing 1/0 silently gets the wrong, unscoped option list - the same "silently wrong list" shape the nameplate enum-scoping ticket exists to fix.
deduped.quote: ?is_busway=true → 3, =false → 29 (correct), but =1 → 32 and =0 → 32 (full unscoped list, no error). Only literal true/false parse.

deduped.title: WO details panel i18n gap: sessions.service and sessions.noDueDate are missing from both locale files, so those two rows render English inline defaults in French
deduped.impact: French users see untranslated "Service" / "No due date" strings in the restored details panel.
deduped.quote: `sessions.service` and `sessions.noDueDate` missing from both locale files → French renders English inline defaults.

deduped.title: Create Work Order wizard's Review step still prints "Scope: starts empty" when the service rules have already resolved assets into scope
deduped.impact: The Review summary contradicts the Scope step ("1 asset — click to edit"), so the creator is told the WO has no scope when it does.
deduped.quote: the wizard's Review step still prints "Scope: starts empty" even when 1 asset is resolved — cosmetic mismatch with the Scope step's "1 asset — click to edit" (worth a cosmetic ticket).

deduped.title: Deleting an account that still has work orders mapped to it is confirmed with the generic "Are you sure you want to delete this item?" dialog - no warning about the affected work orders
deduped.impact: An admin can soft-delete an account with mapped WOs without being told any exist; WO rows keep resolving the deleted account's name, so the destructive action gives no signal at all.
deduped.quote: Deleting an account with mapped WOs succeeds via generic confirm ("Are you sure you want to delete this item?") with no WO-impact warning — soft delete (`/api/account/{id}/soft-delete` → 200)

deduped.title: Create Site dialog has no Account field - the owning account is implied by which account group's "Add Site" button was clicked, so a site is easily created under the wrong account
deduped.impact: Ownership (which now drives WO account stamping and billing attribution) is set invisibly; the QA run itself created the site under the wrong account on the first attempt.
deduped.quote: "Add Site" inherits its account invisibly: Create Site dialog has no Account field; target account implied by which group's "Add Site" was clicked. Easy to create a site under the wrong account (this run did, first attempt).

deduped.title: GET /sld/{sld_id}/library-designations never checks accessible_sld_ids, so the 11-site Facility Manager and 4-site Electrical Engineer read every site's engineering designations
deduped.area: Security / RBAC site scoping · Equipment Designations API
deduped.impact: A site-restricted seat reads asset labels, ratings, kVA, %Z, frame settings and engineering status for sites it is not entitled to see; the sibling PATCH write endpoints likely share the missing check.
deduped.quote: The endpoint filters rows by the `sld_id` in the path and **never checks whether that SLD is in the caller's `accessible_sld_ids`**.

deduped.title: By-id work-order endpoints /ir_session/{id}/full, /team and /summary/v2 return complete payloads for a work order whose site is outside the caller's accessible_sld_ids
deduped.area: Security / RBAC site scoping · Work Order API
deduped.impact: The whole by-id API family trusts the id in the path instead of the token's scope, so any role can read work orders on unassigned sites.
deduped.quote: the already-recorded open finding that `/ir_session/{id}/full`, `/team` and `/summary/v2` return complete payloads for a work order whose site is outside the caller's `accessible_sld_ids`, while the corresponding *list* endpoints scope correctly

deduped.title: The /emps route still renders the old EMPs list after the Sales nav entry was retired
deduped.impact: A page the product means to have retired stays reachable by URL instead of redirecting.
deduped.quote: The Sales nav no longer offers EMPs, but typing `/emps` still loads the old "EMPs · Create EMP" list. If the retirement is meant to be complete, the route should redirect.

deduped.title: GET /sld/{id}/library-designations accepts an unknown kind (?kind=banana) and silently returns the `all` scope instead of a 400

deduped.quote: An unknown `kind` is not rejected: `?kind=banana` silently returns the `all` scope instead of a 400, so a typo in a deep link looks like a working page.

deduped.title: The Sales nav item "Pull-Through Work" is a hard-coded English literal rather than an i18n key, so it stays English in French
deduped.impact: French users see an untranslated menu item, consistent with the two untranslated strings already recorded on the ZP-4088 verdict.
deduped.quote: The Sales nav item is a literal string, not an i18n key, so it stays English in French.

deduped.title: Per-section pricing labels its second option with the unit attribute's own name (e.g. `sections`) instead of the specified "Per section", which is absent from the bundle
deduped.impact: The wording a tester or author is told to look for never appears, so the control reads differently from the spec.
